opening.argument: The title frames this as a live call with alleged tech-support scammers, and a participant tells the caller the exchange is on a livestream. The displayed support page, quoted price, and request for check and bank details are the conduct under examination, not a solicitation directed at viewers. Later, the exchange disputes the caller's Microsoft affiliation and warns that sharing a check exposes its routing, account, and check numbers. Those facts support an investigative account of the call. They do not establish the caller's identity, whether payment was completed, or whether every displayed detail was authentic.

citations.quote: you're on your live stream right now
Type your check number, routing number, account number, and the name on the check.
if you give away your check to anyone the person will have your routing number, account number, and check number as well.
